title: Profiling memory and time on a GPU (with a CPU model of it)

questions.q: Why isn't a job's peak memory just the sum of its tensors?
options: Some tensors die before others are born
Tensors are compressed on the card
VRAM is shared by every model evenly
questions.answer: Some tensors die before others are born
questions.why: The peak depends on what is alive at once. The lab gets 800 or 1100 MB from the same four tensors.

questions.q: nvidia-smi shows most of your card as used, yet nothing is running. What is a likely reason?
options: PyTorch's allocator keeps freed memory in its cache
questions.answer: PyTorch's allocator keeps freed memory in its cache
questions.why: The PyTorch docs say unused memory managed by the allocator still shows as used in nvidia-smi.

questions.q: Why can a stopwatch around GPU code be wrong?
options: GPU operations are asynchronous, so the call may return early
questions.answer: GPU operations are asynchronous, so the call may return early
questions.why: Use torch.cuda.synchronize() before reading the time.

questions.q: Text encoding is 2 s of a 110 s run. How much can making it ten times faster save?
questions.why: You can't save more than a stage takes. Measure first, then attack the largest stage.

questions.q: Five runs: 66, 1.5, 1.5, 1.5, 1.5 s. What is the fair summary of the repeat cost?
questions.why: The first includes loading. The mean mixes a load with the runs.

questions.q: Which tool gives you free VRAM from a running ComfyUI without touching the graph?
questions.why: It reports vram_free and torch_vram_free per device. POST /free would unload things.
